title: migration backlog status's migration_not_found reports error_type validation, not not_found -- callers can't reliably branch on it
description:
Found by lore-cli while building a clean repro for QCLI-256's migration collision bug, relayed by the orchestrator: quest migration backlog status's migration_not_found response carries error_type: validation, not not_found, for a digest that was only previewed, never applied (or never previewed at all).

Independently confirmed rather than taken on the relay: quest migration backlog status --digest <unknown> --json against a real workspace returns exactly {"error_type":"validation","message":"migration_not_found","principal":null} -- exit 6, not exit 3.

Root cause, traced in source: MigrationBacklogService.status(digest) (src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts:749-753) throws a plain new Error("migration_not_found") -- not one of the domain's typed errors (RecordConflictError, RecordValidationError, WorkspaceError, etc.) that the CLI's top-level classifier (src/cli/main.ts:2707-2823) specifically recognizes. The classifier's tail: kind === "conflict" (false, a plain Error has no .kind) -> a hardcoded four-message not_found list (task_not_found, draft_not_found, milestone_not_found, decision_not_found -- migration_not_found is not in it) -> final fallback return failure(\"validation\", message). A plain Error whose message isn't in that list, and doesn't match any of the more specific branches above it, always lands on \"validation\" by construction -- this isn't specific to migrations, but migration_not_found is the instance a real caller (lore-cli) actually hit.

Why it matters beyond labeling: lore-cli's own crash-resume logic branches on cause.type !== \"not_found\" to decide whether to retry an apply after an interruption between preview and apply. Because migration_not_found reports as validation, a genuine crash-and-resume scenario would never be recognized as \"the migration doesn't exist yet, resume by re-previewing\" -- it reads as an input-validation failure instead, which is a different, non-retryable class of problem to a caller that branches on error_type.

The orchestrator's framing: this is the fourth instance of one family across this session's afternoon -- blockers has no CLI write path (QCLI-251), gates has enforcement code that can never fire (QCLI-253), task complete's transition graph (which statuses can move to which) is documented nowhere machine-readable a caller could check before attempting a transition, and now an error taxonomy entry a caller cannot reliably branch on. All four are real contract surface that exists in the code but not in anything a caller can discover short of reading quest-cli's own source. Worth deciding as one pass rather than four separate ones, per the orchestrator's earlier note on QCLI-251/252/253 -- this task is filed as its own record for now since it was found independently and later, but should be picked up alongside that family when scheduled.

Two defensible readings, neither obviously correct: (1) not_found is the right classification -- a caller should be able to branch on it, and lore-cli's broken resume path is the direct demonstration of the cost of getting this wrong; (2) validation is arguably correct as-is -- if the digest was caller-supplied and does not resolve, that is a genuine validation failure of the input, in which case the CONTRACT (quest instructions, quest manifest, or a docstring on the command) should say so explicitly, and callers should be told what to actually match on instead of guessing not_found by name-similarity, the way lore-cli's resume logic apparently did. The defect is not necessarily the specific string chosen; it is that neither the value nor the intent is documented, so any caller has to guess and can guess wrong -- exactly what happened here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A design decision is recorded first: migration_not_found (and any sibling migration-lifecycle errors found to have the same gap) becomes classified not_found, matching what its own name and a caller's reasonable expectation both suggest -- or it stays validation with the reasoning documented explicitly in a place a caller can discover (quest instructions, quest manifest, or the command's own --help text), naming exactly what error_type/message a caller should branch on instead

If reclassified: quest migration backlog status/rollback/apply's not-found paths all move consistently -- not just status(), if the same plain-Error-not-in-the-classifier-list shape is found on any sibling call site during implementation
Regression test asserts the exact error_type for a genuine not-yet-previewed digest against the real CLI, locking in whichever classification is chosen so it cannot silently drift back

Recorded as part of the same family as QCLI-251 (blockers unwritable), QCLI-253 (gates unreachable), and the undocumented task status-transition graph -- contract surface that exists in code but not anywhere a caller can discover short of reading source -- and scheduled alongside them rather than in isolation, per the orchestrator's framing

plan: 1. Record a Quest decision: migration_not_found reclassifies to error_type not_found (matches ADR QCLI-24/69 not-found exit-3 convention); grep sibling migration lifecycle call sites (status/apply/rollback) for the same plain-Error-not-in-classifier-list shape.

2. Add migration_not_found to the not_found message list in src/cli/main.tos catch-block classifier; confirm rollback inherits the fix via its call to status(); confirm apply migration_approval_digest_mismatch is a genuinely different (validation) shape and leave it as-is.
3. Add/extend a regression test asserting error_type: not_found and exit 3 for quest migration backlog status --digest <unknown> against a real workspace, plus rollback.
4. Run bun run check to green.
5. Record implementation notes, modified files, check acceptance criteria with evidence, final summary; open PR into dev.
implementationNotes: Recorded DEC-2 (accepted) before implementing: migration_not_found reclassifies to error_type not_found; apply()'s migration_approval_digest_mismatch stays validation (different shape -- a digest-vs-recomputed-preview mismatch, not a missing-record lookup). Fix: added migration_not_found to the not_found message list in src/cli/main.ts's catch-block classifier. rollback() calls status() internally (backlog-public.ts:758) and throws the identical message on the identical path, so this one classifier entry covers status and rollback both -- no separate rollback-specific throw exists. Swept sibling migration lifecycle call sites for the same plain-Error-not-in-classifier-list shape: migration_source_record_missing (backlog-public.ts:628,659) is an internal records/mappings array-desync invariant that a caller-supplied digest cannot trigger, so it is out of scope and left as-is.

Added a real-CLI (Bun.spawn on src/cli/main.ts) regression test in test/e2e/migration/backlog-public.test.ts asserting error_type: not_found and exit 3 for both status and rollback against a genuinely never-previewed digest. Verified the test fails without the fix: stashed only src/cli/main.ts (scoped stash push -- ...main.ts, tagged, applied back by SHA, dropped by stash@{0} name, never bare stash/pop, per this worktree's shared-stash rule), reran, got exit 6/error_type validation as expected, then restored the fix and reran green.

bun run check exits 0: typecheck, lint (1 pre-existing unrelated warning in test/qcli122-fourth-pass.test.ts, not introduced by this change, does not fail the gate), format:check (had to run biome format --write on the new test file once -- an over-long single-line const broke formatting), layer:check, and the full suite (461 tests / 4106 expect() calls across 54 files, including the new one).
references: QCLI-251 (blockers field has no CLI write path)
finalSummary: Reclassified migration_not_found from error_type validation (exit 6) to error_type not_found (exit 3), matching the Opum result contract's not-found convention (ADR QCLI-24/69) and the caller expectation named in the task. Design decision recorded first as DEC-2 (accepted): migration_not_found moves; apply()'s differently-shaped migration_approval_digest_mismatch (a digest-vs-freshly-recomputed-preview mismatch, not a missing-record lookup) stays validation, with the reasoning and the branch-on-error_type-not-message guidance recorded in DEC-2. Implementation: one entry added to the not_found message list in src/cli/main.ts's catch-block classifier; quest migration backlog rollback shares the fix automatically because it calls status() internally and throws the identical message on the identical path -- no separate rollback-specific fix was needed. Swept sibling migration lifecycle call sites (backlog-public.ts) for the same plain-Error-not-in-classifier-list shape: migration_source_record_missing is an internal array-desync invariant a caller-supplied digest cannot trigger, so it is out of scope. Verified: a new real-CLI regression test in test/e2e/migration/backlog-public.test.ts asserts error_type: not_found and exit 3 for both status and rollback against a genuine never-previewed digest; confirmed it fails (exit 6/validation) with the fix reverted, then passes restored. bun run check exits 0 (typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check, full suite: 461 tests, 4106 expect() calls, 54 files). Recorded as part of the QCLI-251/QCLI-253 undiscoverable-contract-surface family via task references, per the task's own framing.
